summary: Twin-towered Bakers Island Light has marked the approach to Salem Harbor since 1798; the second tower went dark in 1926 and the station is now run by Essex Heritage.

access.note: The island is private; the public reaches the light station only on Essex Heritage's boat tours (landing craft Naumkeag from Salem Ferry Dock), overnights or volunteer days.

The first keeper was Captain George Chapman of the Salem Marine Society. He served until 1815, when he was about 75 years old. Chapman later became blind, a condition that was blamed on the brightness of the lighthouse lamps.
George Chapman (1798-1815)
Joseph Perkins, who received a federal commission as a pilot in 1791, was on Baker’s Island during the War of 1812.
Perkins rowed out in his dory, boarded “Old Ironsides,” and deftly guided the frigate to the safety of Marblehead Harbor.
Captain Perkins has a garden enclosed, three cows, six pigs, and was cutting hay for the winter.
The Reverend Dr. William Bentley visited Perkins at the lighthouse in August 1817.
Near the end of March in 1825, Keeper Nathaniel Ward and his assistant, a Mr. Marshall, left the mainland in a small flat-bottomed boat laden with wood and other supplies, heading for the island.
Ward was later found dead on the shore of the island, and Marshall died in the boat. According to a newspaper account, Ward was 49 years old and left a large family
In late October 1825, a squall claimed the lives of both Keeper Nathaniel Ward and his assistant Mr. Marshall.

Ambrose Martin followed Ward as keeper at a salary of $300 yearly, raised to $400 in 1829. Martin’s daughter Jane, who learned to help her father tend the station, later became keeper at Marblehead Light.

The assistant keeper beginning in 1872 was Walter Scott Rogers of neighboring Beverly. When Rogers took the assistant position, he was in poor health and weighed only 101 pounds. He became the principal keeper in 1874

by the time he left for West Chop Light on Martha’s Vineyard in 1881. He returned to Baker's Island in 1892 for another 11-year stint as keeper. In 1894, he recorded as many as 500 visitors to the light station in one day.

Rogers reported in February 1875 that the harbors of Salem and Beverly were frozen solid as far as Baker’s Island. When the ice broke up, it piled as high as 15 feet.
During a particularly bad stretch of fog in October 1876, Baker’s Island’s fog bell was sounded for 72 straight hours.
Rogers had assisted in 21 wrecks during his years at Baker’s Island, and he had saved the lives of six men. He had furnished more than 400 meals for shipwrecked mariners.
Keeper Rogers retired to a farm in Rowley, Massachusetts, in October 1911.

notes_for_editor: Story rests mostly on two secondary web histories (D'Entremont, LighthouseFriends), which agree on most points but differ on: Ward's death (March vs October 1825), which twin light was higher, tower height (59 vs 47 ft), lens year (1857 vs 1855 archive), siren date (12 vs 8 July 1907), and Martin's term (archive to 1850; NEL to 1843). Lewis, Bentley and the 1816 notice are quoted via New England Lighthouses, not read in the original. The archive's USLHS place record shows coordinates for Maine (44.24,-68.20), which are wrong; the match is by name and 'Salem, Essex Co., MA'. Roster dates are the archive's; lines like 'Red Dawson (1940s-)' are kept with approximate years. The USCG-heading keeper Paul J. Baptiste (1946-1951) is also in D'Entremont's list. Hadley/Terpeny/Rogers 'other_stations' come from New England Lighthouses. Bakers Island, Mass. is not Baker Island, Maine, which dominates the corpus hits (Life-Saving Service reports and the 1912 Bulletin illuminant item are Maine and were not used). No newspaper hits found for Terpeny/Baker's Island 1894-95 on Chronicling America. A search snippet said the original lens was 'returned to the light station in 2026' (USLHS); the cached page did not carry it, so it is left out. Not written: NRHP listing year (nomination form OCR illegible); 1976 comes only from the record and the 76-prefixed reference. Characteristic and range come from the record only and are omitted.
